prior_summary: One full-task diffusion policy learns Cartesian TCP command poses in a causal adaptive lid/peg/target reference. This makes lid approach/opening move with the observed lid, peg approach/lift move with the observed peg, and elevated transport/insertion move with the observed target by construction, while a single unchanged DP backbone models the complete temporal behavior.
applicable_conditions: Use from the normal reset or from an intermediate observed state for the same covered-peg task when lid_pose, peg_pose, hole_pose, target_pose, Panda state and TCP pose are valid. Displacements should remain reachable and preserve the box/lid/peg/hole geometry and collision-free topology represented by the demonstrations.
termination_guidance: Evaluation termination is the supplied task success definition only: the cover has been opened and the peg is turned and inserted with its head in the specified x interval, y/z within 0.009 m of the hole, and axis alignment at least 0.985. Gripper state, reference weight or elapsed time alone is not success.
limitations: Only twelve highly similar successful demonstrations are available. No contact truth is observed, so a closed gripper can be mistaken for a grasp; large pose changes can create collisions or unreachable IK; a lid that fails to open can make the causal reference remain lid-centered; and the smooth reference transition is unsupported for unusual lifted/dropped peg states. Millimetre insertion remains sensitive to observation error, compliance and DDPM sampling. The decoder reports rather than repairs unconverged IK.
